title: Basic Network Troubleshooting
scenario: Mr. Thompson calls the IT Service Desk. His classroom desktop in room 118 cannot reach any websites. The computer shows it is connected to the network with a valid IP address, but browsers show 'DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NO_INTERNET'. Other teachers in nearby classrooms are working normally. He has not changed anything on the machine. Class starts in 15 minutes.
impact: Instructional: A 9th-grade math teacher cannot use web-based lesson materials. The 25 students in his first period will be without the planned digital content until connectivity is restored.
objectives: Identify the affected device, user, and time of onset
Confirm scope: is this one device or multiple?
Run basic network tests from the device (IP, ping, DNS)
Form a hypothesis and choose the least-risky fix
Restore connectivity or escalate with evidence

evidence.description: Output of ipconfig /all showing IP, gateway, and DNS servers
Ping results to gateway and to an external IP (8.8.8.8)
Check network status board and nearby rooms to confirm scope

decisionPoints.prompt: ipconfig shows a valid IP and gateway, ping to the gateway succeeds, ping to 8.8.8.8 fails, and nslookup times out. What is the most likely cause?

options.label: DNS resolution is broken — the machine can reach the network and external IPs but cannot resolve names
options.feedback: Correct — the signature is clear: ping by IP works, but name resolution fails. DNS is the broken layer.

options.label: The school's internet uplink is down
options.feedback: If the uplink were down, ping to 8.8.8.8 would also fail. The scope check (other rooms working) also rules out a wide outage.

options.label: The Ethernet cable is unplugged or damaged
options.feedback: If the cable were bad, ipconfig would not show a valid IP and gateway. The device is on the network.

decisionPoints.prompt: Which is the correct, least-risky remediation?

options.label: Flush the DNS cache (ipconfig /flushdns) and reconfigure the device to use the school's DNS servers explicitly
options.feedback: Correct — flushing the local cache removes any stale entries, and explicit DNS configuration ensures the device uses the right resolver.

options.label: Re-image the workstation with a standard image
options.feedback: Destructive. A DNS configuration change does not require rebuilding the machine.

options.label: Tell the teacher to use his phone as a hotspot instead
options.feedback: Bypassing the school network does not fix the underlying DNS problem and may introduce security concerns. Restore the school network.

ticket.initialDescription: Classroom desktop in rm. 118 cannot reach websites. 'DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NO_INTERNET'. Other rooms fine. Class in 15 minutes.

nodes.title: Take the call
nodes.body: Take the call. Verify the user, the room, and the time the problem started. Open a P2 ticket. Note that class starts in 15 minutes.

nodes.title: Confirm scope
nodes.body: Check the network status board and call or message a teacher in a nearby room to confirm the issue is isolated to room 118. Document the scope.

nodes.title: Run network diagnostics
nodes.body: Run ipconfig /all, ping the gateway, ping 8.8.8.8, and run nslookup for a known hostname. Save all output to the ticket. Look for the layer at which things break.

nodes.title: Identify the cause
nodes.body: Based on the diagnostics, what is causing the connectivity issue?

nodes.title: Choose the remediation
nodes.body: Pick the least-risky fix to restore connectivity.

nodes.title: Restore DNS
nodes.body: Walk the user (or visit the room) through flushing the DNS cache and confirming the DNS server entries. Test by opening a browser and loading a known site. Document the result.

nodes.title: Validate
nodes.body: Confirm the teacher can reach the lesson site and the school's portal. Confirm the browser no longer shows the DNS error. Have him ready the classroom materials.

nodes.title: Document the fix
nodes.body: Close the ticket with: the failing layer (DNS), the action taken, and the validation evidence. Send a brief follow-up to the teacher.
nodes.prompt: Write a brief follow-up to Mr. Thompson confirming the fix.

nodes.title: Debrief
nodes.body: Review your score. Think about the OSI-layer pattern: when ping by IP works but name lookup fails, DNS is the broken layer.

kbOpportunity: When ping to IP works but websites fail, the broken layer is DNS. Flush DNS cache and confirm DNS server settings before any device rebuild.
